evidence.limitations: Qualitative code review of reusable comparison programs; no cross-language numeric benchmark executed in this unit. Scores are relative expert assessments per language_quality.md guidance (idiomatic best practice, no artificial penalty/boost). No LLM proficiency scenario data generated here; only static code-quality metrics for Rust assessed as assigned.

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.method: Inspected reusable Rust micro-benchmark programs (mb00-mb11) and adversarial programs under template/programs/rust. Assessed token/line density needed to express the same algorithm relative to idiomatic Rust practice: iterator chains (zip, map), no manual bounds-checked indexing loops except where the frozen algorithm requires index-based updates, preallocated Vec<f64>, no unnecessary cloning.
observations: mb04.rs: core workload uses iterator zip over two f64 vectors with four scalar accumulators, concise and idiomatic; avoids manual index loops in the hot inner loop.
Outer loop anti-elimination update (a_vec[r % M] += 1e-9) requires index-based access intrinsic to the algorithm across all languages, not Rust-specific overhead.
No unnecessary heap allocations inside hot loops; vectors preallocated via vec![0.0f64; M].
Ownership/borrowing model enables safe zip-based iteration without bounds-check boilerplate or copies (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]).
Struct-based Lcg generator is compact standard encapsulation; no boilerplate beyond Rust's module/impl requirements.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.score_rationale: Idiomatic iterator/zip patterns keep code compact relative to explicit-index languages; slightly more verbose than Python (types, impl blocks, float suffixes) but comparable to Go/Java/Kotlin. Scored 78/100.

metric.readability.method: Reviewed identifier naming, control flow, and structuring conventions in the reusable Rust programs (micro and adversarial sets) for idiomatic readability: function separation, comments citing methodology sections, meaningful variable names, consistent formatting.
observations: Comments cite exact methodology sections and describe algorithmic intent, aiding traceability.
Explicit local type annotations (f64, usize, i64) improve self-documentation without excessive verbosity.
Explicit .expect()/.unwrap_or() error handling avoids hidden control flow, aiding clarity of paths.
Tuple destructuring (let (s1,s2,s3,s4) = ...) names results clearly, improving clarity over positional/pointer outputs.
Adversarial programs are short, single-purpose files isolating one language-edge-case each, aiding per-file readability.
metric.readability.score_rationale: Strong type system, explicit ownership annotations, and pattern-matching idioms yield self-documenting code with low incidental complexity; on par with Kotlin/Swift, above raw-pointer-heavy C++/Zig styles, though explicit type/lifetime annotations add minor cognitive overhead vs dynamically typed languages. Scored 80/100.
